entities.summary: The Kaiser class was a class of five dreadnought battleships that were built in Germany prior to World War I and served in the Kaiserliche Marine during the war. They were the third class of German dreadnoughts, and the first to feature turbine engines and superfiring turrets. The five ships were Kaiser, Friedrich der Grosse, Kaiserin, Prinzregent Luitpold, and König Albert. As was usual for German battleships of the period, the Kaiser class mounted main guns that were smaller than those of their British rivals: 30.5 cm (12 in), compared to the 34.3 cm (13.5 in) guns of the British Orion class.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Kaiser class battleships played a significant role in the lead-up to World War I, with four of the five ships serving as flagship and flagship's escort during the war. The class's design influenced subsequent German dreadnoughts.
